counts_source: PSNProfiles progress targets (for example 0/42 Shooting Range challenges)
list: The official 55 trophies, as published on PlayStation (via Exophase and PSNProfiles, checked 2026-11-19)
note: Guides are this guide's own words, written from the official descriptions and the PSN progress targets. The game released 19 November 2026; where a specific place or step has not been verified in the game yet, the guide says so plainly.

trophies.guide: The platinum. It unlocks automatically once the other 54 trophies are earned, so there is nothing to do for this one directly — it is the reward for finishing everything else. Track it last: when your checklist reads 54 of 55, this one pops on its own. Plan the run around the roadmap in this guide, and clear the missable trophies on your first playthrough so nothing forces a second full run.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing — the first story mission of the game. It cannot be missed in the sense of failing it (you can retry), but it is a one-time story beat, so play it when it comes and do not skip the opening. This is the earliest trophy most players will earn, and it opens the story path that the chapter trophies follow.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 1 to its end. Chapter trophies unlock as the story advances, so there is no side task here — keep following the story missions in order. Use the chapter as your warm-up for the tracker: get used to checking off trophies as they pop, and start the long-count activities (stunts, vehicles, areas) early, since they build up naturally while you travel between missions.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies, this one comes from story progress alone. By this point the map opens up further, so between missions start banking progress on the exploration trophies — discovering vehicles and visiting new areas of Leonida — rather than rushing straight to the next story marker.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3. Story progress only — no side requirement. Mid-game is a good moment to check the tracker: stranger mission strands (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) and the activity trophies are all available by now, so clear a few of them between story missions instead of leaving them all for the post-game cleanup.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the finale. Before you push into the final mission, sweep up any story-gated missables you have not done yet — the partner robberies, the VCIA departure and the choice-based trophies — because the finale is the natural point of no return for one-time story moments. The chapter itself needs only story progress.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Complete the final story mission. This is the gold trophy for finishing the story, and it unlocks the post-game free roam where most cleanup happens. Do not rush it: finish the missable story trophies first (see the Missables page), because after the finale some one-time story moments may be gone. Once it pops, the remaining work is side content, collectibles and the 100% completion trophy.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. It is a named story mission, so it arrives as part of the plot — play it when it is offered and do not skip it. Named-mission trophies like this one are the reason the roadmap follows the story in order: each mission trophy is earned by playing the mission, and the only way to miss one is to pass its point in the story without doing it, which the game does not normally let you do. The exact chapter this mission sits in has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Trust
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. A heist mission in the story — play it when it unlocks. Heist missions are usually the big set-pieces of a chapter, so expect a longer mission with a setup and a payoff. The trophy is for completion, not for any particular approach, so any way through the mission counts. Its exact place in the chapter order has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Another named story mission — it unlocks as the plot reaches it. There is no extra condition beyond finishing the mission, so play it normally when it appears. If you are tracking the story trophies in order, this one sits among the mid-story mission trophies; its exact chapter has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Family Matters
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. A named story mission that arrives with the plot. Finish it when offered; completion is the only requirement. The mission's name suggests a high-profile target, but the trophy does not ask for a stealth or style condition — just get through it. Its exact chapter has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set around Vice City International Airport. Finish the mission when the story offers it. Note the related trophy Catch Me If You Can, which is about making an unscheduled departure at VCIA — do that one while you are in the airport area for this mission if the chance comes up, since airport access may be tighter outside the mission. The mission's exact chapter has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. A named story mission — play it when it unlocks and finish it. The name suggests a large operation, likely late in the story, so expect it near the end of the chapter run. Completion alone earns the trophy; no special condition is stated in the official description. Its exact chapter has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion — PSN tracks this as a 0/100 counter. This is the gold trophy that gates the platinum, and it is the last one most players will earn. 100% in this series normally means finishing the story, the stranger strands, the activities and the collectibles the game counts toward completion — not every trophy, but a defined checklist the in-game stats screen shows. Work through this guide's roadmap and watch the in-game completion percentage; the exact list of what counts toward 100% has not been verified in-game yet, so follow the game's own stats screen as the authority.
trophies.name: A Long Road
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — PSN tracks a 0/250 counter. Stunts are the game's driving tricks: jumps, near misses, drifts and airtime, the kind of thing that happens naturally while driving fast between missions. Start early and let the count grow: every risky drive adds to it, and grinding all 250 in one sitting at the end is a chore. If the game counts a specific list of stunt types, the in-game stats screen is the authority — the exact definition of a counted stunt has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once — PSN tracks a 0/9 counter. The activities are the game's side pastimes (shooting range, drone races, races, fishing, arcade games, bowling and the others the game offers). You only need to try each one once, not master it, so sample everything early: visit each activity the first time you pass it. Which 9 types the counter counts has not been verified in-game yet — use the in-game activity list as the checklist.
trophies.name: Master of None
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — PSN tracks a 0/42 counter. This is a skill trophy, not a grind: every challenge must be golded, so expect to replay the hard ones. Work through the challenges weapon by weapon, learn each one's scoring, and leave this for a dedicated session rather than squeezing it between story missions. The 42 challenges are spread across the range's disciplines; the exact list of ranges and their locations has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: The Shootist
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at all 14 locations — PSN tracks a 0/14 counter. Drone races are a Top Fun activity: find each of the 14 race locations around Leonida and win at each one. Winning takes a clean run, so learn the course on a practice pass, then race for the win. The locations themselves are the work — the exact 14 spots have not been verified in-game yet, so check the activity marker on the in-game map for each one.
trophies.name: Top Fun
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — PSN tracks a 0/20 counter. 'Different' is the key word: the same race won twice counts once, so you need 20 distinct race events. Work through the race list across the map, and keep a note of which ones you have won. Any vehicle class counts as long as the race is a new one. The full race list and where each starts has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a fishing rival — challenge him and out-fish him. Fishing challenges are usually about catching the bigger or better fish in the time given, so use your best rod and bait and watch the challenge rules on screen. This is flagged missable in this guide because a named rival challenge can be a one-time story-adjacent moment; if the challenge is repeatable from the fishing spots, it is safe — that has not been verified in-game yet, so take the challenge the first time it is offered.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game. Find an arcade machine, start a game and play it to completion — finishing is what counts, not a high score. Arcades are scattered around Leonida; the first machine you find is enough for this trophy. Which arcade titles the game offers, and where the machines are, has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy, one of the stranger mission strands. Stranger strands are chains of side missions for named characters — follow Andy's chain to its last mission. Do the strand when it appears rather than leaving it for the end: strands can be tied to story progress, and their final missions are the ones that can be missed if a strand is never started. Where Andy's strand begins has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Kenton, another stranger strand. Follow Kenton's chain of missions to its end. Like the other stranger finals, the risk is never starting the strand — once you are in the chain, the final mission follows naturally. Start Kenton's missions as soon as they appear on the map. Where the strand begins has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Billy, a stranger strand. Work through Billy's missions to the last one. Stranger strands are easy to overlook while chasing the story, so check the map for stranger markers between chapters and clear them as they appear. Where Billy's strand begins has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands — PSN tracks a 0/8 counter. This is the silver that ties the stranger content together: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and the other strangers each have a strand, and you need 8 finished. Start every strand you find and finish each chain before moving on; the counter is the proof of which ones are done. The full list of stranger strands and their starting points has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Randy, a stranger strand. Follow Randy's chain to its last mission. As with the other stranger finals, the danger is not the mission itself but never starting the strand — check for stranger markers regularly and do them when they appear. Where Randy's strand begins has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Tyrone, a stranger strand. Work through Tyrone's missions to the final one. Start the strand early — stranger chains can unlock in stages as the story advances, so revisit the marker if a later mission does not appear at once. Where Tyrone's strand begins has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida — PSN tracks a 0/18 counter. Meditation spots are quiet places around the map; visit each one and meditate there. This is a pure exploration collectible: the work is finding all 18, so sweep the map region by region and tick them off as you go. The exact 18 spots have not been verified in-game yet — the in-game map markers are the guide here, and this guide does not invent locations.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret sends you after one particular animal — track it, hunt it and bring it down. Unique-animal hunts are usually about finding the right territory and reading the signs, not about combat skill. Take the hunt when Bret offers it; if it is tied to his stranger strand, finishing it may also count toward that strand. Which animal and where it roams has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Fair Game
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets — PSN tracks a 0/3 counter. Collectible cards are scattered around Leonida in sets; a set is complete when you hold every card in it, and you need 3 full sets. This is a long hunt: grab cards whenever you pass a location, and trade or revisit spots for the last few in a set. How many cards a set holds, and where the cards are, has not been verified in-game yet — this guide does not invent card locations.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations — PSN tracks a 0/100 counter. WAiNK It is a location-based activity: find 100 spots around Leonida and do it at each one. Treat it as a map-sweep trophy — work through the regions one at a time and let the count climb as you explore. The exact 100 locations have not been verified in-game yet, and this guide does not invent them; the in-game activity markers are the checklist.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges — PSN tracks a 0/50 counter. Challenges are the game's small objectives across driving, combat, exploration and activities; each finished challenge adds to the count. Play broadly and the counter climbs on its own — try everything, and the 50 will come. Check the in-game challenges menu to see which ones you have done and which are close. The full challenge list has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose the cops and escape. The partner is the key condition — do it during a story moment or free-roam stretch when your partner is with you, not alone. Get to 4 stars (enough heat that helicopters and roadblocks are in play), then break line of sight and stay out of the search area until the stars clear. This is flagged missable because partner availability is story-gated; take the chance while your partner is around.
trophies.name: Hot Together
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner, keeping your wanted level the whole time — do not lose the heat between robberies. Plan a route of three close shops, rob each in turn and keep moving; the trick is speed, because the wanted level must stay live from the first robbery to the third. Do it with your partner present, while the story still has you working together. The exact shop route has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — PSN tracks a 0/100 counter. 'Discover' means finding a new vehicle type, so variety is what counts: drive, steal and sit in as many different cars, bikes, boats and aircraft as you can. Every new model you get into adds to the count. Sweep parking lots, traffic and the roads between missions, and check the in-game vehicle list for what you have found. The full vehicle list has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the game's slow-down aiming mode — trigger it in a busy fight and drop 5 enemies before it ends. Pick a fight with plenty of enemies close together, and make every shot count while time is slowed. If you fail, retry the same fight: the condition is one use, five takedowns. How Combat Focus is triggered and how long it lasts has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport — leave the airport in a way that is not a scheduled flight. In plain terms: steal a plane or otherwise take off from VCIA on your own terms. Do it while you are at the airport for the VCIA Takedown mission if the chance comes up, since airport access may be tighter in free roam. This is flagged missable because it is tied to one location and one kind of moment. The exact method that counts has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Deal with the Rhinos — the tanks. The description is a joke, and the trophy is about an encounter with Rhino tanks: expect a military or high-heat moment where Rhinos show up, and survive or destroy them. The official description gives no number and no method, so the honest guide is: when tanks appear, engage them and stay alive. Which encounter counts, and how many Rhinos it takes, has not been verified in-game yet — this guide does not guess.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a clean, stealthy robbery. Plan it: case the store, go in quiet, take the goods and leave before anyone raises the alarm. Detection is the fail condition, so slow is fast here — if you are spotted, leave and try again rather than shooting your way out. Which jewelry store counts, and whether the game offers more than one, has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape — PSN tracks a 0/5 counter. Bank vault robberies are the big jobs: break into the vault, take the money and get out clean. You need 5 of them, so treat each one as a planned heist with an escape route, not a smash-and-grab. The vault locations and how each robbery opens up have not been verified in-game yet — the in-game map and story will point to them.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks travel the roads of Leonida — intercept one, crack it open, take the money and lose the wanted level that follows. The escape is part of the trophy, so have a fast car and a route out before you start. Trucks appear in traffic; the exact spawn pattern has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida — PSN tracks a 0/52 counter. This is the map-completion trophy: visit every named area of the state, from Vice City's districts to the countryside and the coast. Drive through each area until the counter ticks; the in-game map shows which areas you have been to. Sweep region by region in the post-game, when fast travel and free roam make it easy. The 52 area names have not been verified in-game yet — the in-game map is the checklist.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs — PSN tracks a 0/9 counter. Every gang in Leonida runs illegal operations; hit one operation per gang, all 9. This is a map-wide hunt, so keep a note of which gangs you have hit — one per gang is enough, and hitting the same gang twice does not help. The 9 gangs and their operation locations have not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Pest Control
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Find a bar or beach spot on Ocean Beach, order a cocktail and take in the view — a quiet moment trophy, not a challenge. It is flagged missable in this guide only because it is tied to one specific place and one specific act; the spot itself should still be there in free roam. Which bar or spot counts has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight through the showroom glass and out the other side, the series' signature move. Pick a showroom, get a fast car inside or aimed at it, and go through the front. The trophy is for the style of the exit, so make it dramatic. Which showroom counts has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — play a game of bowling there. 'Follow-through' is the bowling term for completing your throw, so the trophy is about playing a frame properly at this specific alley, not about a score. Visit the Kolt & Associates alley, bowl a game and finish it. Where the alley is has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: A partnership moment with mass appeal. The description is deliberately vague — it points at a story moment between the two partners that the public notices. Play the story and watch for a partnership beat that draws a crowd; it is likely a specific mission or scene, and the trophy pops when it happens. Flagged missable because it reads like a one-time story moment. Which scene it is has not been verified in-game yet — this guide does not guess.
trophies.name: Personal Best
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Make choices — PSN tracks a 0/500 counter. The game counts choices you make, and you need 500 of them. This is a long-tail trophy: every dialogue option, decision and branching moment adds up, so play naturally and make choices whenever the game offers them instead of skipping through. It will finish late in a full playthrough. What exactly counts as a 'choice' has not been verified in-game yet — the in-game counter is the authority.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Second time's the charm — succeed on a second try. The description points at failing something once and then succeeding: retry a failed mission, challenge or attempt and clear it on the second go. It will likely pop on its own during a normal playthrough, since everyone fails something eventually. If it has not popped by the end, deliberately fail and retry a short challenge. What exactly counts has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the game's odd, secret moment. The description is a joke about an unexpected event, the kind of hidden encounter this series hides in the world: a strange sight, a weird NPC or an easter egg. Explore off the beaten path, especially at odd hours and in remote places, and the moment will find you. What the event is, and where, has not been verified in-game yet — this guide does not invent it.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by — hit a pedestrian with a melee weapon while driving past. Drive slowly through a crowded area, lean out and swing as you pass. It is a single, deliberate act: one hit is enough. Pick a busy street, keep your speed low so the swing connects, and do it away from heavy police presence. The exact weapon and speed that count have not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts — PSN tracks a 0/250,000 counter. Marked Bills are dirty money from robberies and heists; your contacts clean them for a cut, and the cleaned total counts toward the $250,000. Keep laundering after every big job instead of letting bills pile up. Which contacts launder bills, and their rates, have not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — PSN tracks a 0/100,000 counter. Buy weapons, clothes, cars, food and everything else the shops sell; every dollar spent anywhere counts. This finishes naturally if you gear up properly through the game, but if you are frugal, spend the endgame on cars and property upgrades. Track it in the in-game stats. Shop prices and the cheapest way to the total have not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties — PSN tracks a 0/8 counter. Garages are properties you buy to store vehicles; there are 8 of them around Leonida. Save money through the game and buy them as they become available — they are also useful, since they give you somewhere to keep the 100 vehicles you need to discover. The 8 garage locations and prices have not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — PSN tracks a 0/10 counter. Scooter Bros is the in-game app for registering vehicles: take 10 different vehicles, open the app and register each one. Any vehicle you drive can be registered, so do it as you discover new vehicles for the Whip It Good trophy — the two trophies pair naturally. How the app's registration works has not been verified in-game yet.
trophies.name: On the Spot
sources: Guide note: our own advice from the official description; not yet verified in-game
